message: i feel stressed but i love the feeling of the calming spirit of my heavenly father and the feeling to keep working
second_note: Best alternative: love, expressed toward the heavenly father and his calming presence; fear also fits the stress. Sorrow is not expressed.

second_note: love is plausible from the gaze and smile, but joy also fits the playful encouragement without clear romantic context.

message: i am still feeling a bit dull from the loss of sleep and am trying to sleep in each morning as possible

message: im polyamorous something im starting to feel truly accepted for being
second_note: love is defensible as feeling accepted, but joy better captures the positive experience of self-acceptance and belonging.

message: i had that kinda feeling but ignored it
second_note: Lexical cue: ignored refers to dismissing a feeling, not the writer being neglected. The emotion itself is unspecified.

message: i have a feeling itll be a little more messy going home though
second_note: Anticipating a messy return could support sadness, but fear about forthcoming complications is at least as plausible.

message: i reread for comfort the familiarity of a book whose plot i already know is easier to deal with when im feeling stressed than a new to me book with all its unknowns
second_note: Best alternative: fear; stress and seeking predictability to avoid unknowns express anxiety rather than sorrow.

message: i feel agitated with myself that i did not foresee her frustrations earlier leading to the ending of our relationship
first_note: follows 'agitated'; reads as anger at self or sadness
second_note: Agitation can support fear, but anger at oneself for failing to anticipate the breakup is at least as strong.

message: i really feel like having my own space anymore is a really vain idea
second_note: The belief that having personal space is futile expresses discouragement.

message: i have been feeling really stressed out due to homework and my studies that have increased rapidly over the last week
second_note: Best alternative: fear; the message expresses academic stress and pressure without sorrow or grief.

message: i am feeling very indecisive and spontaneous
second_note: Indecision can support fear, while spontaneity can suggest joy; neither emotional reading is established by this short message.

message: i feel completely distracted and emotionally drained
second_note: Best alternative: sadness; emotional depletion is expressed without anger or frustration toward anyone.

message: i did feel slightly weird in that costume
second_note: fear is plausible as self-conscious unease, but surprise at unfamiliar feelings in the costume is also possible; weird is underspecified.

message: ive blogged and i feel strange about it
second_note: Lexical cue: strange describes discomfort about blogging, not sudden amazement; fear is the closest alternative for unease.

message: i feel very saddened that the king whom i once quite respected as far as monarchs go was ineffectual at best
second_note: Lexical cue: respected describes the writer's former opinion of the king; sadness is explicitly expressed by very saddened.

message: i still do feel left out i do feel like the most hated kid in the asian crew
second_note: Lexical cue: hated describes others' attitude toward the writer; sadness best captures feeling left out and rejected.

message: i feel blessed beyond blessed to share my life with you each week
second_note: The direct appreciation of sharing life with the addressee expresses affection.

message: i journaled about my tendency to sometimes overcommit myself which can make me feel exhausted and overwhelmed
second_note: Exhaustion supports sadness, while being overwhelmed by commitments also supports fear as anxiety or stress.

message: i don t know how else to describe it except to say that i had the same feeling about three weeks before my beloved grandmother passed away
first_note: foreboding; follows 'beloved'; reads as fear or sadness
second_note: Best alternative: sadness for the bereavement context, or fear if the unspecified feeling is a premonition; happiness is unsupported.

message: i guess no matter how much i think im feeling ok im as nervous as hell on the inside about the scan revealing something i dont want to know again
second_note: Lexical cue: okay is an apparent state explicitly overridden by being nervous as hell; fear clearly dominates.

message: i can t quite figure out how i feel i m not devastated like i was with lucy and i m not sure if that s because it s easier to do after the first time or what
second_note: Lexical cue: devastated is negated for the current feeling and refers to a previous experience; the current emotion is explicitly uncertain.

message: i hate feeling like this this is bullshit ok i m so done bye

message: i walked to school he felt the bounce in his step the overjoyed feelings of youth and the thrill of excitement of coming to school and meeting his beloved friends

first_note: cold towards a partner: anger or sadness
second_note: Lexical cue: cold means emotional detachment and lost affection, not strong displeasure; sadness is the closest alternative for the troubled relationship.

message: i feel fake because i think if you really want to have a good conversation and make good contact you have to appear especially self confident and even risk talking to some people which are no good to talk to at all until you meet one person which you have a good connection to

message: i decide that picking the easy route would get me nowhere and i feel like other people want me tortured so i follow the blue path

message: i replied feeling strange at giving the orders

message: i woke up and felt sad all over again but that was quickly replaced with a feeling that reassured me things will work themselves out on their own time
second_note: The narrative explicitly replaces sadness with reassurance and a positive outlook.

message: i think we were both feeling a little drained from work as well
second_note: Lexical cue: drained describes tiredness after work rather than sorrow. None of the six emotions is clearly established.

message: i just keep on feeling blessed
second_note: Lexical cue: blessed expresses general gratitude without an object of affection; joy is the literal best fit.

message: im afraid to call the guy from yesterday because i think hell be angry because i think my boss is angry because i dont communicate with him and i feel like im doing a shitty job and i project my fears onto him
